bib.title: OlympiadBench: A Challenging Benchmark for Promoting AGI with Olympiad-Level Bilingual Multimodal Scientific Problems

read.skipped: References skimmed only; figure pages 22-23 (IPhO example) are image-heavy text

question: Can a hard, bilingual, multimodal Olympiad-level math and physics benchmark with auto-scorable answers separate current LLMs and LMMs, which saturate GSM8K and MATH?
hypothesis: Existing math and physics benchmarks are too easy and text-only; Olympiad-level problems will be far harder for frontier models and widen gaps between them.
contributions: OlympiadBench: 8,476 Olympiad-level math and physics problems (incl. Chinese college entrance exam) with expert step-by-step solutions
An automatic scoring pipeline (SymPy-based) for numeric, expression, equation, interval and tuple answers
Evaluation of GPT-4V, Gemini-Pro-Vision, Qwen-VL-Max, Yi-VL-34B, LLaVA-NeXT-34B, DeepSeekMath-7B-RL, GPT-4 and an error analysis of GPT-4V

method.summary: Problems from international and Chinese Olympiads and Gaokao mocks were OCRed (Mathpix) to markdown, checked manually, deduplicated by embedding cosine similarity, and hand-labelled by subfield and answer type. Models are evaluated zero-shot with one prompt template on the open-ended, auto-scorable subset; answers extracted from \boxed{} and judged by a SymPy-based pipeline; metric is micro-average accuracy.
method.task: Olympiad-level math and physics problem solving (open-ended, bilingual, multimodal)

datasets.name: OlympiadBench
datasets.size: 8,476 problems (6,142 math, 2,334 physics); 4,869 (57%) with images; 6,728 open-ended (79%), 1,748 theorem proving (21%); EN 2,125, ZH 6,351; CEE:COMP 66%:34%
datasets.split: Full experiments on open-ended problems with auto-scorable answer types; theorem proving only manually sampled for GPT-4V
datasets.source: Official Olympiad PDFs (IMO, RMM, ARML, EMC, EGMO, IPhO, APhO, EPhO, USAPhO, PUPC, OPhO), Chinese regional/national competitions, Gaokao mock questions from Wisdom Way AI Lab; GitHub OpenBMB/OlympiadBench
datasets.preprocessing: Mathpix OCR to markdown, manual verification against PDF, Problem-Solution-Answer structure, dedup via cosine similarity with a small math LM (Laurie/Bloom1b7-deepspeed-chat-Chinese-math), manual labels for subfield and answer type; progressive physics problems merged into a context field. Avg question 253 tokens, max 3,745; avg solution 347, max 4,223 (images excluded).

other.note: requires a specific CoT prompt appended to input; text-only

inference.samples: one response per problem; no repeats or seeds stated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot; one fixed template for all models, no per-model prompt engineering; template states subject, answer type(s) and the required closing sentence 'So the final answer is \boxed{answer}.'; knowledge points from the dataset not included in prompt; DeepSeekMath-7B-RL gets its own CoT suffix

other.unavailable_responses: removed from accuracy; <1% except Qwen-VL-Max Physics-En_COMP where 26 questions exceeded max input length
other.image_input: LLaVA-NeXT-34B and Yi-VL-34B accept a single image only

metrics.name: micro-average accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of problems whose extracted final answer is judged equivalent to ground truth by the auto-scoring pipeline (numeric tolerance default 1e-8, adjustable per physics problem; SymPy subtraction approaching zero for expressions; equations moved to one side; intervals/tuples element-wise)

eval.protocol: Auto-scored on open-ended problems; manual sampling of GPT-4V for 164 failed open-ended problems (97 math: 55 EN, 42 ZH; 67 physics) for error types and 81 math ZH_COMP proof problems; no significance tests or repeats stated.

prompts.text: The following is a question from an International <subject> competition. Please calculate the answer according to the given requirements and the information provided. Please use LaTeX format to represent the variables and formulas used in the solution process and results. Please end your solution with [answer-type line] and give the result explicitly. Answer-type lines: single answer: 'The answer of the question should be <ans_type>.'; multiple answers single type: 'The question has multiple answers, each of them should be <ans_type>.'; multiple answers: 'The question has multiple answers, with the answers in order being <ans_type>, ...<ans_type>.' Closing: 'So the final answer is \boxed{answer}.' or 'So the final answer is \boxed{multiple answers connected with commas}.' (Chinese version parallel; reconstructed from Fig 3 text)

results.quote: the precision is manually set as 1e1

limits: Theorem-proving problems (21% of the data) cannot be auto-scored; only sampled manually for GPT-4V

Auto-scorer judges only the two inputs and cannot use problem-specific constraints; cannot judge equality of forms like a*sqrt(b) vs sqrt(a^2 b); tolerance for physics set manually when no official precision exists, so some correct answers are marked wrong
Annotation is manual and costly, which limits diversity and difficulty
Single zero-shot prompt per model, no decoding settings, no repeats, no variance reported; error analysis covers GPT-4V only (164 problems)
Some closed-model responses missing (<1%, but 26 Qwen-VL-Max physics questions exceeded input length); missing items removed from accuracy
Model versions (2023-2024 GPT-4V, Gemini-Pro) are dated; frontier reasoning models have since moved far beyond 17.97% (not shown in paper)
